ozet: At the gate of Logic Castle, Piko teaches the program to make decisions: if, elif, else, indentation rules, and combining conditions with and, or and in.

giris.anlatim: Day 9: Conditions! In this lesson you'll teach your program to make decisions with if, elif and else, learn the indentation rules, and combine conditions.

cikis.anlatim: The interactive version of this lesson is waiting for you at 30gunde.com.tr. Write your code right in the browser, run it instantly, and finish the tasks!
maddeler: Write and run code in your browser
Learn Python step by step in 30 days

sahneler.anlatim: Hi, I'm Piko! We've reached Logic Castle. Its gate only opens for those who have the key! In games everything runs on rules: when your health runs out, the game is over. Today we write those rules in Python.

if means if. When the condition is True, the line under it runs. else means otherwise. Watch out for two things: the colon at the end of the line, and the four-space indent. What if there were no key? The gate would stay locked.
When there are more than two cases, we use elif: else if. Python checks from top to bottom and runs the first block that's true. Forty-five isn't more than seventy, but it is more than thirty.
Indentation matters a lot in Python. It looks at the spaces to know which lines belong to the if. In most editors, type a colon and press Enter, and the indent appears by itself.

maddeler: The first true block runs, the rest are skipped

sahneler.anlatim: You can combine conditions with and, or and not. Here both must be true: the age is thirteen or more, and less than twenty. Try it with different ages.

How old are you? 15
You're a teen!

sahneler.anlatim: Forgetting the colon is the most common mistake. Python says SyntaxError and even tells you what it expected: a colon! If you forget the indent, you'll get an IndentationError too.
You can write conditions with lists too. There's no key in the bag, but there is a sword. What do you think this code prints?
Ready for battle! The first condition was false, because there's no key. The second condition was true, and Python never even looked at the else.

In the tasks you'll open the castle gate, build a health meter, and combine two conditions for a treasure chest. In the stage task, health shows up as hearts. And in the challenge you'll pick a game mode based on age.
Today we taught our program to make decisions. Now it can take different paths based on rules, just like a game.
